claims.head: Heavyweight bout
claims.body: The Rangers are near the top of the league for the power play, but the Ducks are near the top at the penalty kill. Our lean: the Rangers’ power play wins out. Power plays usually beat kills in these spots. Anaheim’s penalty kill has been near the bottom of the league for years.

claims.head: A shadow job for Miller, Kartye and Lafrenière
claims.call: The Rangers’ L2 (Miller, Kartye and Lafrenière) spends at least 45% of its 5-on-5 time against the Ducks’ first line.
claims.body: At home, the Rangers keep sending Miller’s line (Miller, Kartye and Lafrenière) out against opponents’ first lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Mike Sullivan has been giving this group the hard job of facing the other team’s top line. Tonight the Ducks’ first line is Killorn, Carlsson and Klepov.

notes.text: The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 7 games cover only 31% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the 6th-lowest in the league (a typical team: 45%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.
Troy Terry is on long-term injured reserve and has not played this season. He is one of their most valuable skaters.
Mikael Granlund is day to day (upper-body injury) and missed their last game. He is a top-six forward.
Spencer Martin was added to the roster on Oct 14.
Justin Dowling was added to the roster on Oct 15 and has played beside Oliver Bjorkstrand and Jaroslav Chmelař.
Sean Durzi has started killing penalties: on the ice for 43% of the team’s shorthanded time in 9 games, up from 7% with his old team last season.

NYR.head: Leaning the Rangers’ way
NYR.body: Even though Anaheim has been out-chancing opponents lately, the Ducks will be without Terry, and the Rangers have home-ice advantage. Still, it’s close: the Ducks can make it interesting if they keep the shots coming.

ANA.head: The Ducks start a half-step behind
ANA.body: Even though Anaheim has been out-chancing opponents lately, the Ducks will be without Terry, and the Rangers have home-ice advantage. The Ducks’ best way to tip it is piling up shots.
